topic: Physical and Chemical Changes from Temperature
key_concepts: A physical change changes appearance or state without forming a new substance.
A chemical change forms a new substance and is usually irreversible.
Melting ice and boiling water are physical changes because water remains water.
Burning wood or charcoal forms ash and new substances, so it is a chemical change.
Boiling an egg is a chemical change because it cannot change back into a raw egg.
Freezing is the change from liquid to solid at the freezing point.
Melting is the change from solid to liquid at the melting point.
Boiling is the change from liquid to gas at the boiling point.
Physical change indicators include change in shape, size, or phase.
Chemical change indicators include gas production, smell change, and unnatural color chang
Reversible changes allow the original state to return, such as ice melting and refreezing.
Burning paper forms ash, a new substance, so it is an irreversible chemical change.
